headline: Still completely dry through the 72-hour window, so the street stays at none; today's 12:35 PM king tide (about 10.6 ft with surge) is the hazard, on the Bay shore only, and NWS has trimmed Sunday's rain to a light 0.10 to 0.25 in.

summary.text: Down for Sunday: NWS now expects only 0.10 to 0.25 in away from the mountains (was 0.25 to 1 in), and calls the first system unimpressive. The stronger storm shifts to Tuesday into Wednesday.
Wettest 3 hours, next 72 h: NBM, ECMWF, GFS and HRRR 15-minute all 0.00 in. HRRR and RRFS hourly series are missing from this snapshot.
Rating card consensus 0.00 in (NBM only; HRRR and RRFS missing): none. Yellow (garage) would need about 0.71 in in 3 hours; Sunday's models show under 0.1 in.
Dry through Saturday. Light rain arrives Sunday from about 5 AM, steadiest Sunday afternoon and evening. NWS's more impactful storm is Tuesday into Wednesday.
King tide today 9.4 ft at 12:35 PM, NOAA model about 10.6 ft near 1 PM. Friday 9.1 ft at 1:28 PM (about 10.4 ft). Channel at Alameda 0.12 ft, far below Monitoring 3.18 ft.
Nothing needed on the street. Avoid the Bay shore and shoreline roads about 11 AM to 2 PM today and Friday. Clear drain grates before Sunday.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text:
Quiet Thanksgiving morning under building high pressure, with high clouds streaming in from the northwest and patchy fog in a few inland valleys. NWS San Francisco (12:16 AM discussion) expects warmer, drier weather through Saturday, with highs in the mid to upper 60s, a few interior spots near 70.

The storm door stays open. NWS now describes Sunday's system as weak: beneficial rain, 0.5 to 1.00 in in the coastal mountains but generally 0.10 to 0.25 in elsewhere, cooler air behind it, and a 15 to 20 % chance of thunderstorms only north of Point Reyes. A second, more impactful storm arrives Tuesday into Wednesday with moderate to heavy rain and strong winds; the GFS brings the low into the Bay Area while the ECMWF takes it into the Central Coast, and the NWS forecast currently keeps the heaviest totals over the Central Coast. That storm is beyond the window this page's models cover.

The Coastal Flood Warning for San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines (reissued 11:54 PM Wednesday) runs until 4 PM today.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since the 4:20 PM Wednesday discussion nothing has changed in the next 72 hours: every available model is still dry. The change is in the outlook just beyond: NWS lowered its Sunday estimate for cities around the Bay from 0.25 to 1 in to 0.10 to 0.25 in, and the second storm is now framed as Tuesday into Wednesday rather than late Monday into Tuesday.

Wettest 3 hours / total, from 4 AM Thursday (72 hours, to 4 AM Sunday):
• HRRR hourly: no data in this snapshot.
• RRFS: no data in this snapshot.
• HRRR 15-minute (ends 11:45 PM Fri): 0.00 in.
• NBM: 0.00 / 0.00 in.
• ECMWF: 0.00 / 0.00 in.
• GFS: 0.00 / 0.00 in.

Just past the window, Sunday's light rain is now in the series: NBM about 0.22 in for Sunday (wettest 3 hours 0.05 in), ECMWF about 0.17 in (0.07 in), GFS about 0.10 in (0.06 in, early Sunday evening). That is well within what the street drains handle.

Consensus: with HRRR and RRFS missing, the rating card falls back on NBM at 0.00 in, none. Every global model agrees, so the missing high-resolution runs do not change the picture for the next three days.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (run ends 1 AM Saturday) is running about 0.9 to 1.5 ft above the predicted tides at Redwood City, slightly less than yesterday afternoon.

Today: the 7.1 ft high at 2:08 AM came in near 8.5 ft on the model; 3.3 ft low at 7:06 AM (about 4.3 ft); the 9.4 ft king tide at 12:35 PM is modeled at about 10.6 ft near 1 PM (yesterday's run had about 10.8 ft); -1.6 ft low at 8:06 PM (about -0.6 ft near 8:45 PM). Friday: 7.1 ft high at 3:02 AM (about 8.3 ft) and 9.1 ft high at 1:28 PM (about 10.4 ft near 1:45 PM). Saturday's 8.6 ft high is at 2:27 PM and Sunday's 7.9 ft high at 3:33 PM, past the end of the model run.

NWS: at the San Francisco gauge highs are expected 2.2 ft above normal today (8.0 ft MLLW at 11:38 AM), approaching the highest tide ever recorded, and 2.0 ft above normal Friday (12:31 PM) and Saturday (1:28 PM), with up to 1.5 ft of surge and up to 2.5 ft of inundation possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Inundation trends down through the weekend. These tides matter for the Bay shore and tidal sloughs, not directly for Athlone Terrace; with no rain they will not back up the channel at the street. By Sunday's light rain the afternoon high is lower (7.9 ft predicted).

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas 0.12 ft at 4 AM, flat between 0.10 and 0.14 ft for the past day (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft, Watch 4.6 ft, Warning 5.65 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 PM Wednesday, its latest report (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry and calm. The Caltrain rain gauge's latest report (5:13 PM Wednesday) showed no rain in the preceding 24 hours; that station has reported only every 12 hours or so lately (5:13 AM and 5:13 PM Wednesday). The Alameda channel gauge, which reports hourly, is steady at base flow. NWS notes high clouds overhead have limited fog so far near San Francisco Bay.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Very low for the next three days. Sunday's rain looks light in every model and in the NWS forecast. The real uncertainty is the Tuesday to Wednesday storm: a GFS-style track into the Bay Area would bring heavier rain here than the ECMWF's Central Coast track, and NWS mentions possible training rain bands and a Wind Advisory. The missing HRRR and RRFS runs and the Caltrain gauges' long reporting gaps are worth watching before then.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Today and Friday: nothing needed on the street; no need to move cars out of the cul-de-sac. Stay away from the Bay shore, tidal sloughs, piers and low shoreline roads around 11 AM to 2 PM, and don't walk or drive through moving water.
• Friday and Saturday: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains and secure outdoor decorations before Sunday's light rain.
• Early next week: check sandbags and flashlights, and keep this page open Tuesday, when the stronger storm and possible strong winds arrive; power outages can slow the pumps.
